$comment: The class of every string field of every client request, client notification and answer to a server request, with its reason: `free` (a lone surrogate there is read as U+FFFD) or `refused` (a lone surrogate there refuses the frame). It is the independent statement src/free_text.rs FREE_TEXT must equal: the contract test (tests/it/contract.rs every_string_field_is_classed_once_and_free_text_is_listed_free) fails on a field of the schema in no class or in two, a classed field the schema does not have, and any difference between the `free` fields here and FREE_TEXT, either way. Fields are pointers into the payload; `*` is any one array index or map key, a last `{}` the keys of the map there, a last `**` every value and key below. `payloads` enumerates, for each value the schema leaves untyped, the string fields its reader reads (`fields`, or the `schema` definition it deserialises into), with that reader as `source`; `open` names a part that has no fixed fields by nature (JSON a model, a tool, a provider or the language-server protocol wrote, or a setting value whose shape its path decides) with its class and reason: only such a part may be classed whole as `**`. How it was derived: by hand, field by field, not from FREE_TEXT. The string fields come from the protocol schema (schema/client_request.json, client_notification.json, server_request_methods.json; the contract test walks the same files), and for a value the schema leaves untyped from the code of the core that reads it (`payloads` names that code as `source`; LSP params from the methods Node allows and the LSP 3.17 specification). Each field's class was decided from what that reader, and the Node code it ports, does with the string: looked up, matched, run, parsed, sent as an address or a header, or compared with a file or a store -> refused; shown, stored or written as text and compared with nothing -> free; where a recording shows what Node does with a lone unit there, the recording decides and the reason names it. FREE_TEXT was then written to this list and is checked against it, not the other way round: a field added to the schema is in no class until a person classes it here, and the test fails meanwhile.

classes.reason: A Goal's objective, typed or as a `/goal` command.

A model call run on the desktop: the conversation's text, a model's output, a tool's description and schema, a provider's error text; forwarded to and from the provider, never compared (model and tool names, ids and provider state stay refused).
A patch's text (file content), given to `git apply`.
A person's answer to a tool approval or a question (the decision itself is `approved`/`response`, an enum).
A server's arguments and environment values as a person typed them (the names stay identifiers): given to the server's process as Node's spawn gave them (U+FFFD).
A skill's name is checked to `[a-z0-9-]` (mixdog-mcp skills.rs `validate_name`): one that held a lone unit is refused by that check with Node's message, as Node's was.
Commit messages, given to git as Node's spawn gave them (U+FFFD).

File content being written: the workspace refuses it with Node's message (mixdog-workspace fsops.rs `check_paired`); a document's text as an editor holds it. A save's expected content is file text too: the workspace marks one that held a lone unit, and it equals no file Node would have saved over (a lossless file never holds one): refused at Node's comparison with Node's sentence (mixdog-workspace fsops.rs `expected_text`; recorded, native/core/fixtures/inbound-lone-surrogate).

Search queries: a plain-text workspace one matches nothing, as Node's matched nothing (mixdog-workspace textsearch.rs, search.rs); the others search for U+FFFD, the documented difference (decisions.md); git gets what Node's spawn gave it.
Text stored as written: notes, personas, definitions, instructions, prompts, descriptions.
Text typed into a remote browser page or a terminal, written to the page or the pty as UTF-8 (Node's write gave the unit as U+FFFD too); a log line.
The text of a turn, a steer or a queued message (the steer and the queue send turn/start's input), a `/goal` command typed in the composer, the composer's text handed back with a queued entry.
Titles, names and renames shown as typed (the record's id is separate).
A passphrase, password or code a person typed for ssh's question: written to ssh's askpass answer as UTF-8, where Node's write gave U+FFFD too; the answer is never compared or shown.

Values a person types into a form. A workflow's inputs: a JSON body. A custom provider's extra body fields: a JSON body, whose size the core measures as Node's JSON.stringify does, each lone unit as its six-character escape (mixdog-ai providers/custom/config.rs normalize_request_body). A custom provider's header values: Node's check refuses a value outside Latin-1 with `[custom-provider] headers.<name> has an invalid value`, and the core's check refuses U+FFFD with the same text before anything is sent (normalize_headers). A probed MCP server's header values: never sent, any header is configured authentication, Node and the core answer {auth: configured}. Recorded: native/core/fixtures/lone-surrogate-wire (custom-*-header-lone, custom-*-body-*, mcp-probe-header-lone).
What a page or a model shows: visualize tab labels, titles and inline content, a page's title and error.

What the desktop publishes as text: a web page's title (a page may set one holding a lone unit), an import's or the updater's error message, a monitor's name, the text of a Computer Use reply (the model reads it as the tool's result), what a human-only hold is for (the model reads it in Computer Use's refusal), an app window's title and a bridge reply (the model reads them as the tool's result), a Computer Use command the live harness sends (its text and keys are what the model typed).

A link copied from a conversation (a model's markdown link: its href or decoded path) and the session's folder it is resolved against: resolved to a host path as the desktop's transcript-file-links.ts resolved it, which never refused a lone unit (one resolves as U+FFFD and names no file).

A file name, path or text the desktop hands to the PC's file system as given: a chat link to a file under a project (the project folder, the href, the path the user confirmed), an attachment written from a data URL and its name, the launch record file, a user file and the text written into it. Node's fs and path calls took them without refusing a lone unit.
a URL, host, domain, port or transport, parsed and matched
a close reason code the phone's WebRTC stack writes
a duration, parsed into a number of milliseconds; text holding a lone unit is no duration and Node refused it in the same parser

a file's name: compared with a folder's entries before a file is made or opened, or the name of a file the client read from disk; a name holding a lone unit names no file Node would have found (decisions.md "frame-lone-surrogate")
a git ref, commit, tag or config key, or a worktree name that becomes a branch and folder name: matched against the repository; git and Node's ref checks refuse a ref that is not well-formed text
a git ref, commit, tag or label: matched against the repository, whose ref checks refuse a ref that is not well-formed text
a kind, mode, scope, phase, sort, state or other word from a fixed vocabulary the reader matches, written by the client app, never typed text

a map's key: an id, a name or a parameter the reader looks the value up by (an environment variable, a header, an attachment or a model parameter); a key is never typed text, and two keys that read as one would overwrite each other
a model, provider, route, effort, tool, connector, plugin, workflow or agent id from a catalog, matched against it
a path, or a file, command or record name compared with what is on disk or in a store: a name holding a lone unit names nothing Node would have found (decisions.md "frame-lone-surrogate")
a phone's machine-written account of a reconnect (phase, state and issue tokens); the core keeps only [A-Za-z0-9_=@:. -] of it for its log

a provider's raw model record, kept as given
a provider's raw usage object (counts and provider keys), kept as given
a provider's raw usage object, kept as given
a pull-request number

a secret, token or credential name: compared by the service that issued it, never shown; a pasted secret holding a lone unit is not the secret (Node sent the escape as given, UTF-8 conversion makes it U+FFFD), so the request is refused with the field named rather than sending a different secret
a selector of files (glob or path), compared with file names
a setting value at any path, of any shape: the relay-writable paths (RELAY_SETTING_PATHS, service.rs) hold booleans and enums, the others ids and scopes; no setting the clients write is typed text
a sign-in address or a secret sent to a service as it is: compared by that service, never shown as text
a time, date, duration, version or schedule field, parsed into a number or matched against a fixed form
a tool, model, provider or parameter id that the core matches against its catalog or tool list; the text a person reads beside it (displayName, description, label) is listed as free text
an effort level or output style id from a fixed list
an executable path run as a process: a path, not text
an id, cursor, revision or digest the core, a client or a service generated: matched against its record, never typed text
an image's bytes (base64) and the metadata line the resize wrote from it, not typed text
as config/value/write /value
compared with the file's content on disk (the stale-content check): a lone unit there equalled nothing in Node; read as U+FFFD it would equal a real U+FFFD, so it is refused
encoded bytes or a media type (base64, data URL, SDP), decoded, not text
host-only (an agent queue entry's context): a connection's request carrying it is invalidParams before any check of its text
provider-owned continuation state (cache names, response ids, account ids) that the providers compare with their own; it never holds typed text
provider-owned continuation state, as modelProxy/run /call/request/options/providerState
the client app's own name, a constant of the shipped client

an MCP server's header value becomes a header on every request to the server: refused naming the field, nothing saved (decisions.md "Lone UTF-16 surrogates in client strings"). Node saves the server and its fetch refuses the value when it connects (`Cannot convert argument to a ByteString ...`), sending nothing; the core's refusal without side effect is the accepted difference (recorded: native/core/fixtures/lone-surrogate-wire mcp-add-header-lone, mcp-save-header-lone)

Language-server params a person reads or a document receives as given: an item's detail, documentation, label details and tooltips, a code action's title and disabled reason, a command's title, a call-hierarchy item's detail, a signature's label and documentation, and the new text of an edit (insert text, text edits, workspace-edit text and change annotations). The server shows them or writes them into a document and compares them with nothing; Node sent a lone unit there as its JSON escape and the core sends U+FFFD, the replacement glyph either way (decisions.md "frame-lone-surrogate").

Language-server params that carry document text, a message or a label, sent back as the editor holds them: a trigger or typed character (the character typed into the document), a completion item's label, sort and filter text and commit characters, an inlay hint's label parts, a signature parameter's label, and a diagnostic's source, message and related message (the shipped editor sends `marker.message` in every code action request, apps/desktop/src/renderer/editor-lsp-providers.ts, and a diagnostic may quote document text). Node forwards a lone unit as its JSON escape and the server reads it; the core forwards U+FFFD, the replacement glyph either way (decisions.md "frame-lone-surrogate"; recorded: native/core/fixtures/lone-surrogate-wire lsp-code-action-diagnostic-lone)

a language-server identifier or command: a rename's new name (the identifier written into the code), a workspace-symbol query (a symbol name matched against the server's identifiers), a command (run by the server) and a call-hierarchy item's name (the symbol it names). Node forwards a lone unit as its JSON escape to the server, which looks it up or runs it; read as U+FFFD it would name something else, so the request is refused (recorded: native/core/fixtures/lone-surrogate-wire lsp-rename-lone, lsp-workspace-symbol-lone, lsp-execute-command-lone)

a language-server URI, token, result id or annotation id (a document, a work-done or partial-result token, a semantic-tokens result, a workspace edit's document or annotation keys): an address the server resolves, never typed text
a diagnostic's code, its description link and its related information's location, sent back in a code action request: an identifier and URIs the server matches or resolves, never typed text

a language-server word from a fixed vocabulary (a markup kind, a code action kind or `only` filter, a resource operation kind) or a formatting option's name and value: matched by the server, never typed text
language-server data the server wrote or runs, sent back whole (an item's or diagnostic's `data`, a command's arguments): opaque to the client, looked up or executed by the server

What a web page or a page's script shows: its title, a dialog's message and default prompt, a fault text, an element's name and value, a heading, the page text excerpt, an exception text, a snapshot warning, a replaced response body, an init script the agent wrote: shown to the model, compared with nothing; and the page data the engine reads whole (an evaluated value, page text, a CDP result, cookies, storage entries, performance metrics, CDP event params) and the tool-call arguments of the test hook.

an id, cursor, revision or digest the host or the core generated for the engine lane (page, tab, session, document, snapshot, lease, frame, receiver key, element ref, rule, script and download ids, a blob digest): matched against its record, never typed text
a URL, origin, link, file name, file path or URL pattern, parsed and matched (a page's url, a download's file, an intercept rule's pattern)

a kind, mode, state, role, tag, reason code, mime type, method name, accept list, locale, time zone, user agent, color scheme or other word from a fixed vocabulary, or a header name or value, written by the host app or an enum of the lane, never typed text
encoded bytes or a media type (base64, data URL, SDP), decoded, not text (a screenshot's base64 data)
